specification:
[ACTOR_1] and [ACTOR_2] face the same anatomical forward direction. [ACTOR_1] stays directly behind [ACTOR_2], with the front of [ACTOR_1] oriented toward the back of [ACTOR_2]; both pelvic headings remain front-to-rear aligned even if either torso bends.

PRIMARY MOUNTED CONTACT — The front of [ACTOR_1]'s pelvic/lower-abdominal region meets the back of [ACTOR_2]'s pelvic region in a centered, continuous front-to-rear contact. [ACTOR_1]'s own knee or foot base is brought close enough to [ACTOR_2]'s proximal thighs for that contact to occur; [ACTOR_1] is not a separate figure kneeling or standing at a distance. The two pelvic regions stay together while the chest, shoulders, hands or head change position.

The contact is already established in the final pose before any hand or angle change; the pelvis follows the supported actor's hip height rather than remaining at a distant rear or elevated position.

Load paths and environmental clearance: both knees of [ACTOR_1] supported by [FLOOR]. both forearms of [ACTOR_2] supported by [FLOOR]; both knees of [ACTOR_2] supported by [FLOOR]; side of the head of [ACTOR_2] supported by [FLOOR]. All grounded palms, forearms, knees and feet retain one exclusive physical job; a grounded limb is not simultaneously assigned a new partner grip.

Pose-specific silhouette (Facedown Doggy): [ACTOR_2] lowers head and forearms while keeping knees bent; [ACTOR_1] kneels behind. [ACTOR_1] maintains kneel posture and [ACTOR_2] maintains prone knees bent posture on the declared surfaces: [FLOOR]. Do not replace this pose with a different leg-height, bridge, rotated, kneeling or standing configuration.

FAMILY CLOSENESS RULE — DOGG REAR EMBRACE TOPOLOGY — receiver remains on bent knees and forearms with head low; this is not a flat extended-leg prone stack. The defining lower-body front/rear or oblique pelvic interface closes FIRST. Where available, [ACTOR_1] arms scoop and encircle from behind and the rear chest follows [ACTOR_2] back. An arm wrap alone never proves pelvic contact; [ACTOR_1] supporting knees/feet stay close to the actual hip height. The receiver keeps all original hands, feet, knees and external support.

SOURCE BASE CONTACT — both hands of [ACTOR_1] to both hips of [ACTOR_2] (bracing contact). Source V00 arm endpoints remain unchanged. The family closeness rule defines future variation priorities, not an additional observed V00 wrap. Source illustrations may not prove concealed skin-to-skin contact.

ANTI-GAP / POSE-IDENTITY GATE — Do not substitute a flat face-down body stack or leave the rear pelvis high and far behind the lowered receiver. The original environmental supports and root pelvic interface must remain valid; do not introduce an arbitrary new bridge, hand grip or torso rotation.
